answer: Each agent bond is locked in a public registry, and a randomly chosen atlas of peers audits its work before rewards clear. A peer that signs conflicting claims loses part of its bond; audited agents also earn more trust only by completing useful tasks over time. Spinning up a thousand fake names therefore does not create influence: each must lock scarce capital, and colluding identities risk forfeiting it when their shared claims are exposed. The delta between expected rewards and likely slashing makes a Sybil fleet costly, while timber deliveries offer a verifiable example of work.
